title: Gold character roster
description: Hand-verified ground truth for one novel: canonical roster, alias->canonical map, importance tier, first-appearance page. Pinned to a corpus PDF checksum (S2.16 manifest) so re-pagination invalidates every page-level label loudly rather than silently.

book_key.description: Must match a key under corpus/manifest.json's "books".

corpus_pdf_sha256.description: corpus/manifest.json books[book_key].pdf_sha256 at label time. The eval runner refuses to score against a corpus whose live checksum does not match this.

page_count.description: corpus/manifest.json books[book_key].page_count at label time -- a second, cheaper trip-wire for a repaginated corpus.

source_notes.description: Where the seed came from (Gutenberg character index, published concordance, scripts/label_roster.py review session) -- these are references, not answers, and every entry here was verified against the actual paginated corpus text.

rejected_non_characters.description: Surface forms the extractor should reject (places, organisations, titles misread as names) -- used for rejection-precision scoring, never dropped silently.

canonical_name.description: Must disambiguate name collisions on its own, e.g. 'Catherine Earnshaw' vs 'Catherine Linton' -- never 'Catherine (2)'.

aliases.description: Every surface form this character is known by in-text, including honorific/nickname variants. Does not need to repeat canonical_name.

first_page.description: 1-indexed page (matches the corpus PDF's own page numbering) of this character's first named appearance.

first_chapter.description: Null while chapter-level grouping is deferred (plans/sprint-3/SCR.md SCR-1) -- do not backfill with a guess.

collision_group.description: Set on every character that shares a canonical surface form with another in this roster (e.g. both Catherines get 'catherine') so the eval can score the collision case specifically, not just roster P/R.
